_comment: COUPLING tier-2, FSI. Establishes that a partitioned fluid-structure interaction runs end to end through the public `couple` tool across two codes (FEniCSx ALE Navier-Stokes fluid under the conda fenics interpreter, scikit-fem plane-strain structure under the repo venv), on non-matching interface discretisations (49 fluid points against 41 structure ones), and that BOTH DIRECTIONS carry physics. Six configurations. (1) cross-code two-way: converged 19 iterations, validation empty, interface equilibrium 2.62e-04 (x) / 7.38e-04 (y) componentwise, kinematic continuity 3.48e-12 / 4.08e-11 componentwise, and 2.20e-10 relative L2 against a Newton-Krylov re-solve of the same coupled interface equation handed to couple(monolithic=). (2) same-code control with the structure in FEniCSx instead: the two structure codes agree to 2.27e-05 relative L2 on the whole converged interface profile, so the answer is not an artefact of one of them. (3) structure->fluid suppressed (the fluid stops moving its mesh), which is also the rigid-wall configuration where the closed forms bite: net interface force (29.674, 148.183) against plane Poiseuille's (30, 150) and deflection 1.149524e-02 against clamped-clamped beam theory's 1.1375e-02. Suppressing that direction moves the converged deflection by 8.4984e-02 relative, and couple's own interface-sensitivity probe catches the suppression unprompted (the fluid's S collapses to the response floor). (4) fluid->structure suppressed: the deflection collapses to exactly zero and the force balance breaks. (5) a run truncated at 3 iterations under tol=2e-1, which reports converged and is then FAR from the Newton-Krylov root — without it the agreement in (1) would be unfalsifiable. (6) THE LIMIT, run rather than argued: the whole traction convention flipped in the fluid, both in the load the structure applies and in the flux the conservation check sees. That run converges, balances exactly, and the shared-script reference agrees with it to solver tolerance, because the reference drives the same flipped scripts. The structure deflects the wrong way and only the closed form on the undeformed configuration separates it. The added-mass instability is measured separately (see the fsi pitfall group); it is not in this fixture because it is a property of the transient problem and this one is steady.

_mutation.note: Give the fluid participant a viscosity 25% away from the one the closed forms in FsiCase are computed from. The COUPLING is untouched: it converges, both directions still work, equilibrium and kinematic continuity still hold to the same tolerances, the same-code control still agrees, and the Newton-Krylov reference still lands on the root — because every one of those checks is internally consistent with whatever problem the two scripts actually solved. Only the plane-Poiseuille handle on the rigid-wall configuration sees it, and it sees it as 25% in both the normal and the tangential net interface force. That is the whole reason a closed-form anchor is in this fixture at all.

Halve the Young's modulus the structure participant is configured with while leaving FsiCase.e_mod — which the Euler-Bernoulli handle is computed from — alone. The structure then deflects about twice as far under the same load. Everything internal still agrees: the coupling converges, the force transfer balances, the two structure codes still agree with each other because BOTH get the halved modulus, and the reference still finds the root. The clamped-clamped beam estimate is the only thing that separates the softened structure from the one the fixture says it is running.

Pin the fluid's mesh motion off in every configuration, so the structure->fluid direction never exists. This is the mutation that matters most for what this fixture claims: it turns a two-way FSI into a rigid-wall flow solve with a structure bolted on the side, which is exactly the thing that must never be reported as FSI. Three checks die on it, independently: kinematic continuity (the fluid imposes zero where the structure has moved), the Newton-Krylov reference (the coupled root is not the rigid-wall answer), and reverse_direction_is_active (the two-way and suppressed deflections become identical, so the measured effect of the reverse direction goes to zero).
